title: Cross-region eviction threshold ripple analysis and remediation
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Summary: On 2026-02-28 during a marketing-driven token-promotion burst, user traffic spiked in US-West and EU-West. The serving cluster experienced cascading eviction events in the hot-KV cache layer which amplified per-request latency and triggered asymmetric circuit breakers in secondary regions. Result: ~18 minutes of elevated p95/p99 tail latency for text-generation routes and partial degradation of canary routing to Dedicated pools. We missed the p99 SLO for hosted text-generation (target 200ms) for two 5-minute windows, consuming ~27% of the error budget for the week.
impact_timeline: 2026-02-28T09:02:00Z - Promo started; traffic increased 4.3x baseline to generation endpoints
2026-02-28T09:04:30Z - Hot-KV cache eviction rate spike observed on US-West primary serving pods (evict/sec +420%)
2026-02-28T09:06:10Z - Priority-based shed kicked in; lightweight routes were rerouted to secondary regions (EU-West) which had slightly different model variants
2026-02-28T09:07:45Z - Secondary-region circuits tripped due to unexpected connection backpressure; fanout amplified due to sticky affinity reassignments
2026-02-28T09:11:00Z - Engineering mitigation: temporary raise of eviction thresholds, throttle for low-priority background requests, and manual circuit cooldown; latency began to recover
2026-02-28T09:20:00Z - Traffic returned to baseline; post-incident monitoring and trace capture started
root_cause: The immediate root cause was a combination of an underestimated KV-cache working set for the promotion workload and a conservative eviction threshold that caused mass evictions when the working set increased. Evictions led to cache-warmup storms and increased upstream load. Secondary regions received redistributed traffic but had stricter circuit hysteresis and lower connection pool headroom, which caused circuits to trip and created a feedback loop of retries and re-fanout.
contributing_factors: KV cache LRU window not tuned for short, high-QPS bursts
Eviction thresholds were auto-scaled on a slow control loop (60s) and could not react to the 2–5 minute spike
Circuit hysteresis parameters differ across regions and were not aligned with cross-region failover behavior
No dedicated canary rule for promotional traffic; routing preferred primary then sticky fallback instead of parallel probe-based routing
Insufficient observability around per-model KV hit-rates during transient spikes
immediate_actions_taken: Raised KV eviction threshold on affected US-West nodepool (+30%) and initiated a controlled cache-warmup using sampled replay traces
Applied a temporary 20% throttle to bulk/background embed endpoints to free client headroom for latency-sensitive generation requests
Manually relaxed circuit hysteresis in EU-West for 10 minutes to allow gentle ramp of redirected requests
Opened high-priority alerting for KV eviction-rate and cross-region circuit trip count and paged on-call
Captured heap and KV metrics, request traces, and a 10-minute pprof snapshot for offline analysis
notes_from_investigation: Cache warmup storm accounted for ~65% of the excess downstream CPU on inference proxies during the event
Retries caused by tripped circuits generated ~12% additional request volume to the control plane during the window
Secondary regions had 18% lower reserve connection headroom compared to primary due to smaller reserved pool configs
Autoscaler cooldown of 60s for KV pool size prevented immediate scale-up; median reaction time to burst was ~75 seconds
follow_up_action_items: A1: Introduce an adaptive short-window eviction strategy (probe-based) so hot-KV eviction thresholds can rise safely during sub-10min bursts — owner: Priya Gupta — estimate: 5 — due: 2026-04-10
A2: Align circuit hysteresis and connection pool headroom across regions; create a regional baseline matrix and enforce via infra-as-code — owner: Daniel Park — estimate: 3 — due: 2026-03-27
A3: Implement promotional-traffic tagging and a canary routing policy that opens parallel probes to secondary regions before full fanout — owner: Maya Thompson (PM) — estimate: 5 — due: 2026-04-03
A4: Reduce KV autoscaler cooldown from 60s to configurable 10s for short-burst workloads; add safety limits — owner: SRE Team (oncall rotation) — estimate: 4 — due: 2026-03-30
A5: Add per-model short-window KV hit-rate SLO and surface in Console; create an alert that fires on sudden drop >35% in 2 minutes — owner: Observability Team — estimate: 3 — due: 2026-04-06
A6: Create a runbook for controlled cache-warmup (sampled replay + backoff) and link it to the regional failover playbook — owner: Marco Alvarez — estimate: 2 — due: 2026-03-18
A7: Perform an incident load test in staging with 5x baseline token burst across regions to validate mitigations — owner: Reliability Eng — estimate: 5 — due: 2026-04-15
acceptance_criteria_for_fixes: Adaptive eviction reduces median p99 latency during synthetic 4x bursts by 40% versus baseline
Circuit trip count during a staged cross-region failover test remains <= 1 per 10k requests
KV autoscaler reacts to synthetic bursts within 20s in staging
Console surfaces per-model KV hit-rate and fires alerts on 35% drop within 2 minutes
risks_and_open_questions: Adaptive eviction may increase memory pressure in long-running steady-state workloads; need to guard with global caps
Parallel probing to secondaries increases probing traffic; calibrate to avoid repeating amplification
Does reducing autoscaler cooldown risk oscillation in noisy workloads? Need to pair with dampening heuristics
How to prioritize promotional traffic tagging across customers without false positives
